newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Duma to debate budget on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Russian Duma to debate budget on Friday.

text.p: The State Duma lower house of parliament will give the revised 1997 budget draft a first reading on Friday November 22, the Duma speaker said on Tuesday.
Gennady Seleznyov told reporters the house had invited Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin to address the Duma before the debate, but that he had not yet said whether he would accept.

The Duma has already rejected the government's budget once, with deputies complaining on the one hand that revenue projections were unrealistic, and on the other that spending on social programmes and reviving the economy was inadequate.

Since then a reconcilation commission of government officials and representatives of both houses of parliament has agreed a new draft, cutting both revenues and spending, but raising the deficit to 3.8 percent of gross domestic product.
Chernomyrdin will meet leaders of the parties represented in the Duma on Wednesday or Thursday, Seleznyov said.
The Duma's influential Budget Committee will discuss the new draft agreed by the commission on Thursday, and make a recommendation to the full house on whether to pass it.

But senior members of the committee have already said the budget, even in its revised form, may not be passed, and raised the possibility that a 1997 budget will not be passed at all before the start of next year.
The Communist Party, the biggest group in the Duma, will also decide its position on the budget on Thursday, deputy leader Valentin Kuptsov told reporters.
"There's a chance we will vote against this budget if the changes we proposed are not included," Kuptsov said.
"The essence of our position is this: find money for investment and other necessary programmes... even at the cost of issuing more money."
The Central Bank issued a warning on Tuesday that printing money to cover the deficit would simply fuel inflation and accelerate the decline in output but not improve liquidity.
The following are the basic outlines of the budget to be debated on Friday, made available by the Budget Committee.
They differ slightly from those published last week after agreement by the reconciliation commission, as the government had to revise them for technical reasons.
